title: Multi-department Performance Hub
problem: The youth academy's health & performance departments (physiology, medicine, physiotherapy, psychology, nutrition, social work, pedagogy) kept evaluations in separate spreadsheets — no unified per-athlete view, no consolidated report for staff.
targetUser: Academy multidisciplinary staff; two access profiles (regular and admin).
myRole: Sole developer, from import pipeline to deploy.
process: Monolithic Streamlit app with SQLite synced via Google Drive (the database never touches git), a parser pipeline per department running locally or through an import page. Iterated the visuals in short feedback rounds with the real user. Per-athlete PDF engine rebuilt with react-pdf (Node called via Python subprocess) after a first attempt was discarded.
keyDecisions: Streamlit Community Cloud + SQLite on Drive = zero-cost production.
bcrypt auth + login rate limiting (sliding window per IP), with storage kept separate from the main DB (which the sync overwrites).
Full dark theme with an accessibility rule: status color is never text color — icon or badge/pill background only.
Wellness only charts on days with a real GPS session for that athlete — no context-free floating points.
86 pytest cases covering parsers, rate limiting and the PDF bridge.
result: In production, daily use: per-department dashboards, self-service imports, per-athlete PDF validated against hundreds of real athletes, 2-step-confirmed backup/restore.
learned: Three production lessons that became rules: an automated test pipeline approved a visually broken PDF — visually validating the real artifact is non-negotiable; an unanchored .gitignore pattern corrupted vendored packages only in deploy — a clean-clone check became mandatory before pushing; and tab components that hide panels with display:none permanently zero the height of iframe-based charts — I replaced tabs with radio buttons.
